verdict.summary:
# Quick-Drenching Distance from Battery Handling Areas — 29 CFR 1926 Subpart K

## 1. Answer

**25 feet (7.62 m).** Facilities for quick drenching of the eyes and body must be provided **within 25 feet of battery handling areas** under OSHA's construction electrical standard, 29 CFR 1926 Subpart K, as in force on 2026-11-21.

- Governing provision: **29 CFR 1926.441(a)(6)** — "Batteries and battery charging," paragraph (a) "General requirements," subparagraph (6).
- 1926.441 sits in **Subpart K — Electrical**, under the heading "Safety Requirements for Special Equipment" (Subpart K § 1926.400(d): "Safety requirements for special equipment are contained in § 1926.441").

## 2. Controlling text (verbatim)

> **§ 1926.441 Batteries and battery charging.**
> (a) *General requirements.*
> …
> (5) Face shields, aprons, and rubber gloves shall be provided for workers handling acids or batteries.
> **(6) Facilities for quick drenching of the eyes and body shall be provided within 25 feet (7.62 m) of battery handling areas.**
> (7) Facilities shall be provided for flushing and neutralizing spilled electrolyte and for fire protection.

The 25-foot figure appears identically in every edition of the text checked — the current eCFR text of § 1926.441 and of Subpart K, and the GovInfo annual-edition PDFs for 2025, 2020 and 2009 — which is the basis for the effective-date conclusion in § 3.

## 3. Effective-date verification (as in force 2026-11-21)

| Check | Result |
|---|---|
| Subpart K source note | "51 FR 25318, July 11, 1986, unless otherwise noted" — 1926.441 has been in Subpart K since the 1986 rewrite of the construction electrical standard |
| CFR 2009 edition, Subpart K | Contains 1926.441(a)(6) with "within 25 feet (7.62 m)" |
| CFR 2020 edition, Subpart K | Same text |
| CFR 2025 annual edition (vol. 8) | Same text |
| eCFR current text (fetched 2026-11-23) | Same text |
| Amendments to (a)(6) between 2009 and 2026 | None found in any snapshot; the only part-wide change noted is the 2019 nomenclature update (84 FR 21597), which does not touch 1926.441(a)(6) |

**Conclusion:** the provision in force on 2026-11-21 is 1926.441(a)(6) requiring drenching facilities within 25 feet (7.62 m) of battery handling areas.

**Stated caveat:** the eCFR snapshot was captured 2026-11-23, two days after the target date. The 2026-11-21 conclusion therefore rests on (a) textual identity of (a)(6) across the 2009, 2020 and 2025 annual editions plus current eCFR, and (b) absence of any intervening amendment. That is a strong basis but not a dated 2026-11-21 snapshot; if a signed, date-stamped citation is required for a legal filing, pull the eCFR point-in-time query for 2026-11-21 or the then-current annual edition and attach it.

## 4. What the 25 feet measures, and what it does not

- **Measured to the battery handling area, not to a single battery.** The text uses the plural "battery handling areas," so every area where batteries are handled, charged, filled, or serviced needs its own drenching facility within 25 feet. A facility that covers one charging bay but is more than 25 feet from a second bay does not satisfy (a)(6) for that second bay.
- **25 feet is the outer bound.** A facility at exactly 25 feet satisfies the distance requirement. A facility at any distance greater than 25 feet does not, regardless of how quickly a worker could reach it.
- **The standard sets a distance, not a travel time.** Subpart K contains no "10 seconds" travel-time criterion — see § 6.
- **Distance alone is not compliance.** (a)(6) requires the facility be *provided*; (a)(5) requires face shields, aprons and rubber gloves for workers handling acids or batteries; (a)(7) separately requires means for flushing and neutralizing spilled electrolyte and for fire protection. A drenching unit 20 feet away that is blocked by a parked forklift or has no potable water supply is a practical failure even though the tape measure passes.

## 5. Practical compliance procedure for a construction site

1. **Mark the battery handling areas.** Walk the site and identify every location where batteries are handled or charged — charging bays, battery-change stations for lift trucks, temporary power battery rooms. Physically demarcate each with floor marking or signage.
2. **Measure each area separately.** From the perimeter of each marked area, measure the shortest practical route to the nearest quick-drenching facility (eyewash/drench shower or combination unit). Record the distance for each area. Flag every area whose measurement exceeds 25 feet.
3. **Relocate or add units for flagged areas.** Either move the drenching unit so it lands within 25 feet of the flagged area, or install an additional unit dedicated to that area. Relocating the battery handling area is an acceptable alternative if the layout allows.
4. **Verify the access path.** Confirm the path from each area to its unit is unobstructed, marked, and not used for storage or vehicle parking. Confirm the unit's actuator is reachable without stepping over or around equipment.
5. **Verify the water supply and function.** Confirm the unit delivers flushing fluid (potable water) at the required flow, that the heads are capped/protected, and that the unit is inspected and flushed on a documented weekly/periodic schedule. ANSI/ISEA Z358.1-2014 is the recognized equipment-performance reference for drenching units and is the practical basis for the flush-and-inspect interval.
6. **Record and re-verify on layout change.** Log the distance measurement per area with date and initials. Re-measure whenever the site layout, charging locations, or drenching-unit locations change — this is a construction site, and layouts change.
7. **Train.** Confirm workers in each area know where the nearest unit is and how to activate it.

## 6. Why "10 seconds" is NOT the answer here (important distinction)

There is a widely used figure of **10 seconds' travel time** to an eyewash/shower. It does **not** come from 29 CFR 1926 Subpart K. Subpart K's battery provision is a hard **25-foot distance**. The 10-second travel-time criterion originates in **ANSI/ISEA Z358.1** (the consensus equipment standard) and in OSHA's general-industry drenching provision, **29 CFR 1910.151(c)**, as interpreted — neither of which is Subpart K, and 1910.151 does not apply to construction work covered by Part 1926.

This is confirmed by the search record for the Subpart K pages: the strings "10 seconds," "10 seconds' travel time," and "10 seconds' travel time of the battery handling areas" do **not** appear anywhere in the full text of the eCFR § 1926.441 page, the eCFR Subpart K page, or the 2009/2020/2025 annual-edition PDFs. The 25-foot figure, by contrast, is present and explicit in all of them.

**Practical consequence for a safety professional:** design to the stricter of the two where both are relevant. A 25-foot distance is roughly 5–8 seconds of walking for an uninjured worker, so a layout that satisfies the 25-foot rule will normally also satisfy a 10-second travel criterion — but the two are measured differently (straight-line distance to the area vs. travel time along a path), and only the 25-foot rule is the enforceable Subpart K requirement on a construction site. Do not cite "10 seconds" as the 1926.441 requirement; cite 25 feet and use the 10-second/ANSI criterion as a supplementary design goal.

## 7. Adjacent provisions worth citing alongside (not the source of the distance)

- **1926.441(a)(5)** — face shields, aprons, rubber gloves for workers handling acids or batteries.
- **1926.441(a)(7)** — means for flushing and neutralizing spilled electrolyte and for fire protection.
- **1926.441(b)** — charging installations in designated areas; charging apparatus protected from truck damage; vent caps in place and functional during charging.
- **29 CFR 1926.50(c)** (Subpart D, outside the fetched Subpart K grounding, noted for completeness) — first aid must be provided "promptly"; it carries no drenching distance figure and does not displace the specific 25-foot rule in 1926.441(a)(6).

Where a specific provision and a general one both apply, the specific provision (1926.441(a)(6), 25 feet) governs battery handling areas.

## 8. One-line citation for use in a report

> 29 CFR 1926.441(a)(6) (Subpart K — Electrical): "Facilities for quick drenching of the eyes and body shall be provided within 25 feet (7.62 m) of battery handling areas." Text unchanged in the 2009, 2020 and 2025 CFR annual editions and in the current eCFR; in force 2026-11-21.
